# Conventions

Contributors interact with Gitboard primarily through its CLI tool to manage local development workflows.
### Tooling and Environment
Gitboard relies on the presence of standard forge command-line interfaces. A functional development environment requires:
`git` for local repository state and worktree management.
`gh` (GitHub CLI) for GitHub integration.
`glab` (GitLab CLI) for GitLab integration.
### Configuration and Initialization
The tool is initialized via `gitboard init`, which sets up the local environment. Users manage specific behaviors, such as LLM integration, by editing the configuration file located at `~/.config/gitboard/config.yaml`.
### Workflow Synchronization
The standard operational loop involves running `gitboard sync` to fetch the latest status from the remote forges (CI status, MRs/PRs) followed by `gitboard serve` to host the local dashboard. Contributors ensure their local forge authentication is active via `gh auth login` or `glab auth login` to allow Gitboard to triage failed jobs and track open changes effectively.
